paragraphs.text: translated by
1. SPRUNG from tall trees on windy heights, these rollers transport me as they turn upon the table.
paragraphs.original: प्रावेपा मा बृहतो मादयन्ति प्रवातेजा इरिणे वर्वृतानाः ।
paragraphs.translit: prāvepā mā bṛhato mādayanti pravātejā iriṇe varvṛtānāḥ |

paragraphs.text: The enlivening Vibhīdaka has pleased me like the draught of Soma from Mūjavant.
paragraphs.original: सोमस्येव मौजवतस्य भक्षो विभीदको जागृविर्मह्यमच्छान्
paragraphs.translit: somasyeva maujavatasya bhakṣo vibhīdako jāgṛvirmahyamacchān

paragraphs.text: 2. She never vexed me nor was angry with me, but was ever gracious to my friends and me.
paragraphs.original: न मा मिमेथ न जिहीळ एषा शिवा सखिभ्य उत मह्यमासीत् ।
paragraphs.translit: na mā mimetha na jihīḷa eṣā śivā sakhibhya uta mahyamāsīt |

paragraphs.text: For a dice which scored one too much, I drive away my own devoted wife.
paragraphs.original: अक्षस्याहमेकपरस्य हेतोरनुव्रतामप जायामरोधम्
paragraphs.translit: akṣasyāhamekaparasya hetoranuvratāmapa jāyāmarodham

paragraphs.text: 3. My wife drives me away, her mother hates me: the wretched man finds none to give him comfort.
paragraphs.original: द्वेष्टि श्वश्रूरप जाया रुणद्धि न नाथितो विन्दते मर्डितारम् ।
paragraphs.translit: dveṣṭi śvaśrūrapa jāyā ruṇaddhi na nāthito vindate marḍitāram |

paragraphs.text: [They say:] "I find no more use in a gambler than in an aged horse which is for sale."
paragraphs.original: अश्वस्येव जरतो वस्न्यस्य नाहं विन्दामि कितवस्य भोगम्
paragraphs.translit: aśvasyeva jarato vasnyasya nāhaṃ vindāmi kitavasya bhogam

paragraphs.text: 4. Others embrace the wife of him whose riches the victorious dice have coveted:
paragraphs.original: अन्ये जायां परि मृशन्त्यस्य यस्यागृधद्वेदने वाज्यक्षः ।
paragraphs.translit: anye jāyāṃ pari mṛśantyasya yasyāgṛdhadvedane vājyakṣaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Father and mother and brothers say about him [to the landlord's men]: "We know him not: tie him up and take him away."
paragraphs.original: पिता माता भ्रातर एनमाहुर्न जानीमो नयता बद्धमेतम्
paragraphs.translit: pitā mātā bhrātara enamāhurna jānīmo nayatā baddhametam

paragraphs.text: 5. When I resolve "I will not play with them, I will remain behind when my friends [= fellow-gamblers] depart [to play]",
paragraphs.original: यदादीध्ये न दविषाण्येभिः परायद्भ्योऽव हीये सखिभ्यः ।
paragraphs.translit: yadādīdhye na daviṣāṇyebhiḥ parāyadbhyo'va hīye sakhibhyaḥ |

paragraphs.text: and the brown dice, thrown on the board, have rattled, like a fond girl I seek the place of meeting.
paragraphs.original: न्युप्ताश्च बभ्रवो वाचमक्रतँ एमीदेषां निष्कृतं जारिणीव
paragraphs.translit: nyuptāśca babhravo vācamakratam̐ emīdeṣāṃ niṣkṛtaṃ jāriṇīva

paragraphs.text: 6. The gamester seeks the gambling-house, and wonders, his body all afire, "Will I be lucky?"
paragraphs.original: सभामेति कितवः पृच्छमानो जेष्यामीति तन्वा शूशुजानः ।
paragraphs.translit: sabhāmeti kitavaḥ pṛcchamāno jeṣyāmīti tanvā śūśujānaḥ |

paragraphs.text: The dice run against his desire, giving the best throws to his adversary.
paragraphs.original: अक्षासो अस्य वि तिरन्ति कामं प्रतिदीव्ने दधत आ कृतानि
paragraphs.translit: akṣāso asya vi tiranti kāmaṃ pratidīvne dadhata ā kṛtāni

paragraphs.text: 7. Dice, verily, are armed with goads and driving-hooks, deceiving and tormenting, causing grievous woe.
paragraphs.original: अक्षास इदङ्कुशिनो नितोदिनो निकृत्वानस्तपनास्तापयिष्णवः । कुमारदेष्णा जयतः पुनर्हणो मध्वा सम्पृक्ताः कितवस्य बर्हणा
paragraphs.translit: akṣāsa idaṅkuśino nitodino nikṛtvānastapanāstāpayiṣṇavaḥ | kumāradeṣṇā jayataḥ punarhaṇo madhvā sampṛktāḥ kitavasya barhaṇā

paragraphs.text: They give gifts like boys [do], and then snatch them back from the winner,
[they are] sweetened [as] with honey with magic power over the gambler.
8. Their troop of three-times-fifty plays [as undefeatably] as Savitr the god whose ways are faithful.
paragraphs.original: त्रिपञ्चाशः क्रीळति व्रात एषां देव इव सविता सत्यधर्मा ।
paragraphs.translit: tripañcāśaḥ krīḷati vrāta eṣāṃ deva iva savitā satyadharmā |

paragraphs.text: They bend not even to the anger of the mighty: the King himself pays homage and reveres them.
paragraphs.original: उग्रस्य चिन्मन्यवे ना नमन्ते राजा चिदेभ्यो नम इत्कृणोति
paragraphs.translit: ugrasya cinmanyave nā namante rājā cidebhyo nama itkṛṇoti

paragraphs.text: 9. Downward they roll, and then spring quickly upward, and, handless, force the man with hands to serve them.
paragraphs.original: नीचा वर्तन्त उपरि स्फुरन्त्यहस्तासो हस्तवन्तं सहन्ते ।
paragraphs.translit: nīcā vartanta upari sphurantyahastāso hastavantaṃ sahante |

paragraphs.text: Cast on the board, like lumps of magic charcoal, though cold themselves they burn the heart to ashes.
paragraphs.original: दिव्या अङ्गारा इरिणे न्युप्ताः शीताः सन्तो हृदयं निर्दहन्ति
paragraphs.translit: divyā aṅgārā iriṇe nyuptāḥ śītāḥ santo hṛdayaṃ nirdahanti

paragraphs.text: 10. The gambler's wife is left forlorn and wretched: the mother mourns the son who wanders homeless.
paragraphs.original: जाया तप्यते कितवस्य हीना माता पुत्रस्य चरतः क्व स्वित् ।
paragraphs.translit: jāyā tapyate kitavasya hīnā mātā putrasya carataḥ kva svit |

paragraphs.text: In constant fear, in debt, and seeking money, he goes by night to the home of others [probably to steal].
paragraphs.original: ऋणावा बिभ्यद्धनमिच्छमानोऽन्येषामस्तमुप नक्तमेति
paragraphs.translit: ṛṇāvā bibhyaddhanamicchamāno'nyeṣāmastamupa naktameti

paragraphs.text: 11. Sad is the gambler when he sees a woman, another man's wife, and his well-ordered dwelling.
paragraphs.original: स्त्रियं दृष्ट्वाय कितवं ततापान्येषां जायां सुकृतं च योनिम् ।
paragraphs.translit: striyaṃ dṛṣṭvāya kitavaṃ tatāpānyeṣāṃ jāyāṃ sukṛtaṃ ca yonim |

paragraphs.text: He yokes the brown horses [= the dice] in the early morning, and in the evening he sinks down beside [his] fire, a beggar.
paragraphs.original: पूर्वाह्णे अश्वान्युयुजे हि बभ्रून्सो अग्नेरन्ते वृषलः पपाद
paragraphs.translit: pūrvāhṇe aśvānyuyuje hi babhrūnso agnerante vṛṣalaḥ papāda

paragraphs.text: 12. To the great captain of your mighty army [of dice], who has become the host's imperial leader,
paragraphs.original: यो वः सेनानीर्महतो गणस्य राजा व्रातस्य प्रथमो बभूव ।
paragraphs.translit: yo vaḥ senānīrmahato gaṇasya rājā vrātasya prathamo babhūva |

paragraphs.text: To him I show [my] ten [extended fingers]: "I speak the truth: No wealth am I withholding."
paragraphs.original: तस्मै कृणोमि न धना रुणध्मि दशाहं प्राचीस्तदृतं वदामि
paragraphs.translit: tasmai kṛṇomi na dhanā ruṇadhmi daśāhaṃ prācīstadṛtaṃ vadāmi

paragraphs.text: 13. "Play not with dice, [but] cultivate your corn-land. Enjoy the gain, and deem that wealth sufficient.
paragraphs.original: अक्षैर्मा दीव्यः कृषिमित्कृषस्व वित्ते रमस्व बहु मन्यमानः ।
paragraphs.translit: akṣairmā dīvyaḥ kṛṣimitkṛṣasva vitte ramasva bahu manyamānaḥ |

paragraphs.text: There are your cattle, there your wife, O gambler": So this good Savitr himself has told me.
paragraphs.original: तत्र गावः कितव तत्र जाया तन्मे वि चष्टे सवितायमर्यः
paragraphs.translit: tatra gāvaḥ kitava tatra jāyā tanme vi caṣṭe savitāyamaryaḥ

paragraphs.text: 14. Make me your friend: show us some little mercy. Do not forcibly bewitch us with magic power.
paragraphs.original: मित्रं कृणुध्वं खलु मृळता नो मा नो घोरेण चरताभि धृष्णु । नि वो नु मन्युर्विशतामरातिरन्यो बभ्रूणां प्रसितौ न्वस्तु
paragraphs.translit: mitraṃ kṛṇudhvaṃ khalu mṛḷatā no mā no ghoreṇa caratābhi dhṛṣṇu | ni vo nu manyurviśatāmarātiranyo babhrūṇāṃ prasitau nvastu

paragraphs.text: Let your wrath [and] emnity now come to rest. Let the brown [dice] now snare some other captive.
Translation revised 25 April 2006 by
Anthony Appleyard
following Arthur Anthony Macdonnell's book "A Vedic Reader", publ
Motilal Banarsidass
